name: The Aspam household — a name the town's own records carry

division_reconstructed.note: No source places this household anywhere — the record gives a name and no address, no street and not even a division. So BOTH halves of this band are dealt rather than read: the south division from the reconstruction order book's own household target by division, and the class from the town model's employment distribution, which puts this household under the placement policy's merchant_and_professional_dwellings clause. The better houses take the Randolph–Washington tier a block back from the trade, and the north tier under Kinzie: off the noise, on dry ground, with a garden. Inferred — the town holds one documented H roof and it is Cobweb Castle, on the north side, which is itself the clause's own outlier. The deal is seeded on this household's own id, so it is the same on every run — and it is the weakest seat this ladder makes: no lot, no roof, no coordinate and no source behind either half of it.

head: aspam_jean_baptiste

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. church_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 31 October 1833 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1833-10-31 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

basis.note: data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json#arrival_and_origin.tables.arrival_year_of_the_known_layer, restricted to years at or before 1833.

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

reason_for_coming.value: The 1833 season: the harbour appropriation, the treaty at Chicago and the first rush of settlers
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THE SEASON AND NOTHING ELSE. No trade is recorded for this household and no source says why it came; the only thing the evidence gives is when it was here by. This states the draws that were operating in that season and chooses among them nowhere. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

lives_at.note: Not attested: the lists that name this person give no address. The placement sweep assigns homes once the resident list is complete (T-0514, the owner's own sequencing) and this pass will not guess one.

last_dated_appearance.note: A DATED READING OF THIS PERSON, AND THE LAST ONE THE CORPUS HOLDS. Read from `church_evidence` as `1833-10`, which reaches 1833-10-31 — 608 day(s) short of 1835-07-01. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE RECORD DOES NOT REACH THE DAY. Every source that names this person falls on one side of 1 July 1835, and nothing follows them to it or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

sex_basis.note: A DRAW, NOT A READING. Nothing about this person says which sex they were: T-1303 refused the name and was right to. This value is drawn from the measured male share of the roll the person was named on, seeded by their own id so the draw reproduces - retype 'aspam_jean_baptiste:sex_ratio' and the same face comes up. It carries no weight as evidence about this person and it is never promoted. The rate is a ceiling rather than a point reading, because the forename table that settled the rest was built mostly on men's names.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males Under 5', one of its male bands, conditioned on `dependent_child_under_15` because the church register calls the person an infant or a baptised child, or the household record calls them a son, a daughter or a child.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('aspam_jean_baptiste:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: nothing beyond what the record already says: the band is drawn from the schedule's child bands because the record calls them a child. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.
